newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ANGOLA, Jan 21 - Luanda - All general cargo berths occupied, with 2 days delay expected. No delays for container/oil berths. Lobito, Namibe - No berthing delays reported. All crude terminals operating according to programme, with no delays.

ISRAEL, Jan 21 - Haifa - No labour problems. Nine vessels operating of which 5 discharging at berth (2 general cargo, 3 bulkers), 2 container vessels, 2 tankers. 5 Vessels at anchorage of which 2 bulkers waiting to discharge, 2 container vessels, 1 tanker. 2 Vessels under repairs/dry-docked, 2 awaiting orders. 6 Vessels due with 2-3 days delay expected. Ashdod - No labour problems. Fifteen vessels operating of which 12 discharging at berth (11 general cargo, 1 bulker), 3 container vessels. 14 Vessels waiting at anchorage to discharge (14 general cargo, 1 bulker), 2-4 days delay expected for vessels due. Eilat - One bulker loading at berth, 1 passenger vessel, 1 tanker waiting at anchorag

MOZAMBIQUE, Jan 20 - Nacala - Port working normally on a first come-first served basis. No restrictions on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restrictions, 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths, working normally on a first come-first served basis. Container terminal, other terminals - Working normally. Pilotage now possible 24 hours per day for vessels up to 140 metres loa with a maximum draft of 7.5 metres. Two tugs fully operational. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain.

Maputo - Pilotage now possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 120 metres loa with a maximum draft of 9 metres. Two tugs (one out of order). Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangement with the port captain. All berths are working normally and expected to remain so (first come-first served basis). Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres ls 0.5 metres plus the rise of tide.
NAMIBIA, Jan 20 - Walvis Bay - port working normally.

NIGERIA, Jan 21 - Lagos - port working normally/ no berthing delays. Port harcourt - no berthing delays. Bonny, forcados - junior staff employed by shell petroleum develop-ment co., Operators of the bonny and forcados terminal, are reportedly on strike. Their work is being done by senior staff and managers. At present, operations are continuing normally with no delays reported. All other crude terminals worng normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, Jan 20 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths - Working normally. Bulk import berths - Working normally. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.) - Berthing delays of 24-48 hours can be expected for the coming week. One belt export route will be out of service for repairs/upgrading from 06.00 hrs. 27/1 until 18.00 hrs. 1/2. Bulk coal berths - At present 3 vessels at outer anchorage, 4 berthed and 16 due up to and including 27/1. Berthing delays of approx. 24 hours experienced at present. Durban - Container terminal - No delays at present. Point/New pier/Maydon wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) - No vessels for Jan.

Bunker supplies - Fluid. Delays of 8 hours in supplying bunkers can be expected due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - Fully booked for Jan and February. East London - General cargo/combi terminal berths - Busy but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock - Booked from 14/1 to 24/1, then open for bookings. COPPER - Moving in small parcels of 2,500 metric tons per month. Gas oil pipeline - Under utilised. Tankers - Expect to be busy until the end of Jan. Port Elizabeth - Working normally with 4 vessels in port, 8 due this week. No delays expected on general cargo, ore, tanker or container berths.

Cape Town - Breakbulk berths - Working normally. Container terminal - No delays expected for the coming week (weather permitting). Bunker berths - No delays for the coming week. Dry-docks and repair quay - Fully occupied at present, with booking essential. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, Jan 18 - Gabes - Two vessels loading at berth (1 bulk fertiliser, 1 acid tanker), 1 bulk sulphur vessel discharging at berth, no vessels waiting. Sousse - One vessel in port loading bulk cargo, no waiting time. Sfax - Four vessels in port operating of which 3 discharging (2 timber, 1 bulk wheat), 1 loading bulk salt. Tunis - One vessel awaiting instructions, 2 under arrest. 3 Vessels discharging (1 marble chips, 1 wood-pulp, 1 bitumen), 1 vessel in roads awaiting ore crane berth. Rades - One vessel discharging grain, 1 bananas, 2 ro-ro's. La Goulette - North side - 1 Vessel discharging steel coils, 1 general cargo vessel, 1 passenger vessel, 1 ro-ro. South side - 1 Vessel discha

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, Jan 12-18 - Dubai - No labour problems. 182 Vessels of which 81 containers, 10 general cargo, 1 general cargo,container vessel, 6 bulk carriers, 3 car carriers, 18 tankers, 6 naval vessels, 2 U.A.E. naval vessels, 7 bunkering/under repairs/taking stores etc., 5 dhows, 15 barges, tugs, 18 supply boats, 1 lpg tanker, 1 fishing trawler, 1 refrigerator vessel. 4 Container vessels loading at berth, 5 vessels discharging at berth (4 general cargo, 1 tanker), 1 tanker loading at anchorage, 3 general cargo vessels. 7 Tankers under repairs/laid-up, 36 vessels due (28 containers, 4 general cargo, 4 tankers).

YEMEN, Jan 19 - Hodeidah - All berths occupied, 7 vessels berthed of which 2 bulk wheat, 1 wheat flour, 1 containers, 3 general cargo. 2 Vessels anchored of which 1 bulk wheat, 1 sugar. Berthing delays, general cargo up to 2 days delay, bagged cargo up to 4 days delay, bulk cargo up to 6 days delay, containers up to 1 days delay. Mokha - One vessel berthed discharging palm oil, no vessels anchored, no berthing delays.
